model_annotation: This bar chart illustrates the negative log probability of per-specialty medical terms when using the Mistralv0.2-Base model, both before and after fine-tuning on six distinct medical specialties: Cardio (Cardiology), Gastro (Gastroenterology), Infect (Infectious Disease), Neuro (Neurology), Obstetrics, and Pediatrics. The vertical axis represents “Negative log probability,” ranging from approximately -22 to -27, with lower values indicating higher model confidence (i.e., better prediction). The horizontal axis lists the six specialties, each with a group of seven bars: one light blue bar representing the base model’s performance (Mistralv0.2-Base), and six colored bars (light orange, orange, dark orange, brown, dark brown, and black) corresponding to the model fine-tuned on each specialty. In each group, the base model bar is consistently the tallest (highest negative log probability, lowest confidence), while the bar corresponding to fine-tuning on the same specialty as the test set (e.g., “Cardio” fine-tuned model tested on “Cardio” terms) is typically among the shortest (lowest negative log probability, highest confidence), demonstrating improved performance through specialization. The chart visually confirms that fine-tuning on a specific medical domain enhances the model’s ability to predict terms relevant to that domain, with the greatest gains observed in specialties like Neurology and Pediatrics.
